_doc: GB10 GPU, functional model constants. spec = the chip's design or the driver; probe = a microbenchmark that isolates one unit; ablation = a real kernel with one mechanism removed. No value here is fitted to kernel times.

clock_GHz.source: probe: clock.cu, clock64 against globaltimer, 48 blocks of dependent FMAs

tensor_flop_per_clk_per_sm.source: spec: mma.sync m16n8k16 fp16 in, fp32 accumulate; probe mma_rate.cu reached 2.58 TF/s per SM = 1024 x 2.52 GHz with 8+ warps

tensor_eff_pure_mma.source: probe: mma_rate.cu, warps per sub-partition 1 / 2+, two or more independent accumulators per warp

tensor_eff_gemm_loop.source: ablation: noload variants of 22 cp.async kernels at 1024^3, median ideal/measured compute per k-tile by warps per sub-partition (1: n=9, range 0.76-0.88; 2: n=13, range 0.81-0.96); the loss to the pure-mma probe is ldmatrix interleaved with mma in the same warps. 4 per sub-partition not ablated: taken as 2

reg_alloc_unit_per_warp.source: spec: register allocation granularity per warp

l2_effective_bytes.source: probe (round 2): reuse distance at which a re-read stops hitting; 2/3 of the 24 MB (sets and the CPU's share)

port_GBs_per_sm.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu warm L2, 1-32 blocks of 512 threads: 80.7 GB/s each = 32.0 B per clock; TMA (81) and cp.async (76-80) loads alone in the ablations hit the same ceiling

l2_aggregate_GBs.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu warm L2, 48 blocks x 512 threads x 4 loads in flight: 3.47 TB/s (96 blocks: 3.5-4.6)

dram_read_GBs.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu, 64 MB read on a clean L2: 237 GB/s = 87 % of the 273 GB/s spec (256 bits x 8533 MT/s)

lat_l2_ns.source: probe: chase.cu, 16-64 KB, .cg (beyond 1 MB the random chase pays TLB misses, ~400 ns)

lat_dram_ns.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu cold, Little's law at low load: 2-32 KB in flight / measured rate = 436-456 ns

block_issue_us.source: ablation (step 2c): full grid minus 1 block over blocks at 8192^3

block_setup_us.source: ablation: %globaltimer span of an empty block

bubble_us_per_k16_single_block_cpasync.source: ablation: full minus max(compute, loads) per k-tile on the cp.async kernels whose SMs hold one block (0.22 us at block_K 32, 0.39 at 64): per 16-wide k step. With two or more resident blocks it measured 0-0.06: the other block fills it (superseded by cpasync_t0_us, the same mechanism measured directly)

bubble_us_per_ktile_tma_ws.source: ablation (step 2c): full minus max(compute, loads under load) per k-tile at the seven TMA picks, median

dirty_l2_extra_us.source: probe: mlp_stream.cu, MB read after a 256 MB write flush minus after a read flush: the write-back of dirty L2 lines. TileLang's do_bench leaves the L2 this way

cpasync_t0_us.source: WITHDRAWN Oct 20: an artifact of tileload.cu's run-time address division (loopsteps.cu shows no fixed per-k-tile cost); kept only so the analytical model's history is reproducible. probe: tileload.cu, one block of 128-256 threads, 3 stages: time per k-tile = 0.22 us + bytes / 71 GB/s (4 KB 0.275 us ... 24 KB 0.556 us); independent of the stage count (2-5): the loop's serial issue, wait and two barriers, not memory latency. A second resident block fills it (2 blocks/SM: 0.22 + 2 x bytes/71 per round). The ablation's single-block 'bubble' (0.22 us per k-tile at block_K 32) is the same cost

cpasync_r_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, slope of time per k-tile against tile bytes, one block

tma_r_GBs_alone.source: ablation (step 2c): TMA loads-only variant, one block

tma_l2_aggregate_GBs.source: ablation (step 2c): TMA loads-only variant of the 1024^3 pick, 48 blocks, L2-resident: 1.58 TB/s chip

cpasync_l2_aggregate_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, 96-192 blocks (2 per SM), 16 KB tiles, L2-resident: 2.25 TB/s chip

dram_peak_by_segment_GBs.source: probe: tileload.cu, DRAM source, clean L2, 48-96 blocks: 64-byte row segments 201-204 GB/s, 256-byte 230-234; mlp_stream contiguous 237

dram_little_latency_us.source: probe: tileload.cu, DRAM source, 8 blocks x 2 stages x 8 KB: 64 KB in flight at 105 GB/s = 0.62 us (the knee of Little's law; deeper queues raise it)

cpasync_overlap_p.source: ablation: 21 cp.async kernels at 1024^3, each one's whole block time (minus setup) against its compute alone and its loads alone under the full grid; the exponent p with (compute^p + loads^p)^(1/p) = whole has median 1.97 (18 of 21 within 1.5-2.4; three 64x128 tiles overlap almost fully, p 3.7-6). The same warps issue the copies and the mma, so they share issue slots and barriers: balanced parts hide about half of the smaller one, loads 2-4x compute hide 75-86 %. The TMA path, with its own producer warps, overlaps fully (step 2c: max(compute, loads) + sync at every pick)

sim.source: probe: instlat.cu (ldmatrix latency 38.4 cycles per dependent hop incl. the add; ldmatrix 4.0 cycles per x4 per SM with 8+ warps, 11.7 per warp alone; bar.sync 14.6 + ~2 cycles per warp; cp.async 16 B round trip from L2 350 cycles; cp.async 16.0 B per clock per SM within a block = one warp instruction per 32 cycles), mma_rate.cu (HMMA.16816 one per 16 cycles per sub-partition; 29-cycle dependent latency), mlp_stream (DRAM ~0.62 us = 1560 cycles). default_var_latency and rbar_release are assumptions, not measured; cpq.cu: one warp issues a 16 B x 32-lane cp.async every 6 cycles; 4 warps one every 4 cycles per SM (the shared-memory array, 128 B per clock, also used by ldmatrix); 4 warps x 64 copies land at ~64 B per clock per SM (the L2 return path); instlat's earlier 16 B/clk cp.async figure was the probe's own bank conflicts (lanes 128 B apart) and is withdrawn; the chip's L2 serves cp.async tile traffic at 2.25 TB/s with all SMs loading (tileload.cu, 96-192 blocks) = 893 B per clock, shared by the active SMs; loopsteps.cu (Oct 20): TileLang's loop shape (copy, commit, wait, two barriers) with compile-time addressing moves 78 GB/s per SM (30.7 B per clock: the port) up to ~24 SMs; the chip's L2 saturates at 2.07-2.10 TB/s; commit, wait and barriers cost nothing measurable. TileLang's own loads-only kernels confirm 76-80 GB/s with one block. tileload.cu's 37.8 GB/s single-block figure (and the 0.22 us per k-tile fixed cost derived from it) came from run-time integer division in that probe's address code and is withdrawn; the load unit's address stage looks up one 128-byte line per cycle per SM (design assumption, checked: cpq.cu contiguous 512 B = 4 lines -> 4 cycles per copy with 4 warps; predicts the single-block loss of 3 ablated kernels within 20 %); a copy releases its read barrier when that stage has processed it (ncu: the whole kernel gains long_scoreboard 0.80 and mio/lg throttle stalls over its mma-only version); storepat.cu: the two SMs of a pair (TPC) share one store path: every store pattern doubles from 1 to 2 busy SMs and stays flat to 8; TileLang's C store (4 B per lane, 8 rows x 16 B per instruction, half-sectors) takes 15 cycles per instruction (8.7 B per clock), 16 B per lane coalesced 14 cycles per 512 B instruction (37 B per clock); storepat.cu at 24/48/96 blocks: chip-wide store limit ~0.31-0.38 TB/s for TileLang's half-sector 4 B stores and ~1.4-1.5 TB/s for 16 B coalesced stores (the per-pair limit holds to 24 blocks)
